newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria c.bank, banks seen slowing lev fall.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria c.bank, banks seen slowing lev fall.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed between 240-243 per dollar, down from 237-238 in the morning with the central bank and state banks trying to avert a steeper fall, dealers said.
"Increased (forign currency) demand pushed the lev down to 245 in the afternoon but the central bank and three large state banks stepped in to halt the fall amid low supply," a bank dealer said.
The central bank was reported to have sold light dollar volumes between 238-241 lev today, dealers said.
Central bank officials were not available for comment.

A sharp rise in dollar demand pressured the lev to an all-time low of 256 per dollar in very low volumes on Thursday before several state banks launched dollar sales, helping the lev to rebound to 245-247 at the close.

According to some dealers yesterday's sharp lev fall might have been caused by some banks eager to convert into dollars the levs they had received on treasury paper maturity and interest payments this week.
Treasury bills with a total par value of around 6.63 billion levs matured on Wednesday. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
